entries.core_move: Apply the continuous-time Fourier series time-shifting property to convert coefficients for $x(t)$ into coefficients for $x(t - t0)$ by multiplying each $c_k$ by $e^{-jk omega0 t0}$ without recomputing the coefficient integral.
Compute the harmonic-dependent phase change caused by a time shift by subtracting k $\omega$0 t0 from each complex Fourier series coefficient phase while preserving the coefficient magnitudes.
Recognize that time shifting a periodic signal leaves each Fourier series magnitude |$c_k$| unchanged because the time-shift multiplier only rotates coefficient phase.
Update the Fourier series coefficients of a vertically shifted periodic signal by adding the constant offset to the DC coefficient and leaving every nonzero harmonic coefficient unchanged.

Convert the Fourier series coefficients of $x(t)$ to those of $x(-t)$ by replacing each harmonic coefficient with the coefficient at the opposite index and interpreting the spectra as harmonic-index reversals.
Determine how time scaling $x(at)$ changes the fundamental period and angular frequency while reusing the original Fourier coefficient sequence with any sign-induced index reversal.

Infer the negative-harmonic Fourier series coefficients of a real periodic signal from the positive-harmonic coefficients using conjugate symmetry, then translate the relationship into even magnitude and odd phase spectra.

entries.lesson_title: Using Properties Instead of Recomputing Integrals
entries.core_move: Select and apply the appropriate Fourier series property to convert known coefficients into coefficients for a shifted, scaled, reversed, vertically shifted, or real-signal variant without recomputing the coefficient integral.
